strings.campaign.sekigahara.title: Japan — Tokugawa Ieyasu
strings.campaign.sekigahara.subtitle: The Road to Sekigahara, 1598–1600
strings.history.compression_disclosure: This campaign follows real people, places, and major events, but compresses two years into four chapters. Resource totals, troop strengths, and possible outcomes are simulation values designed for play and mathematics.
strings.chapter.1.title: The Balance of Regents
strings.chapter.1.chronicle: Hideyoshi is dead. His young heir remains at Osaka while the regents and magistrates test one another's strength. Every repair, gift, and levy now carries political meaning.
strings.chapter.2.title: The Aizu Question
strings.chapter.2.chronicle: Ishida is out of office and Ieyasu rules in the heir's name, but Uesugi Kagekatsu is fortifying Aizu and refuses to come to court. Ieyasu leads the lords north to punish him. Every formation taken north leaves Edo, its stores and the western roads less guarded.
strings.chapter.3.title: The Western Army Rises
strings.chapter.3.chronicle: Fushimi has fallen and the Western coalition is moving. At Oyama, commanders must decide how to turn west without losing time, food, or one another's confidence.
strings.chapter.4.title: Roads to Mino
strings.chapter.4.chronicle: The armies converge in Mino beneath rain and uncertain banners. What remains in the granaries, treasury, workshops, and council will now become battlefield strength—or absence.

strings.math.c1.labor.prompt: The register lists {total} workers. Assign Farms, Workshops, and Works in a ratio of {ratio0}:{ratio1}:{ratio2}. Enter all three allocations.
strings.math.c1.tax.prompt: The corrected register shows that {percent}% of {whole} households were omitted. How many households were omitted?
strings.math.c1.road.prompt: A road store covers a rectangle {length} sections long and {width} sections wide. One material bundle repairs {coveragePerBundle} square sections. How many bundles are required?
strings.math.c1.letters.prompt: Distribute {total} Treasury among senior houses, military allies, and court messengers in a ratio of {ratio0}:{ratio1}:{ratio2}.
strings.math.c2.provisions.prompt: The quartermaster issues {rationList} Rice to the three formations for each march period. Using these issued rations, how much Rice is required for {travelPeriods} periods? No rounding is needed.
strings.math.c2.perimeter.prompt: Edo's outer depot is {length} sections long and {width} sections wide. How many sections of palisade enclose the whole rectangle?
strings.math.c2.muster.prompt: The rolls list {whole} eligible retainers. The council will muster {percent}%. How many troops will join?
strings.math.c2.allies.prompt: With a budget of {budget} Treasury, choose the affordable envoy plan with the greatest Cohesion gained per Treasury spent.
strings.math.c3.march.prompt: The return route is {distance} distance units. At {distancePerDay} units per day, how many days will the march require?
strings.math.c3.stores.prompt: Each lot costs {lotCost} Treasury and contains {ricePerLot} Rice. With {budget} Treasury, how much Rice can be purchased in complete lots?
strings.math.c3.gifu.prompt: Assign {total} troops between the vanguard and reserve in a ratio of {ratio0}:{ratio1}.
strings.math.c3.relief.prompt: Of {total} Rice, send {firstPercent}% to the northern districts and the remainder elsewhere. Enter both amounts.
strings.math.c4.kobayakawa.prompt: Distribute {total} Treasury among a guarantee, retainer gifts, and messengers in a ratio of {ratio0}:{ratio1}:{ratio2}.
strings.math.kobayakawa_letter.prompt: Your courier must ride {distance} distance units to Kobayakawa's camp. At {distancePerDay} units per day, how many days will the letter take?
strings.math.c4.granaries.prompt: The three formations are issued {rationList} Rice for each battle round. Using these issued rations, how much Rice must the granaries reserve for {rounds} rounds? No rounding is needed.
strings.math.c4.fieldworks.prompt: The fieldwork is {length} sections long and {width} sections wide. Each square section requires {materialsPerSquare} Materials. How many Materials are required?
strings.math.c4.weather.prompt: Each report lists reliability and predicted rain. Multiply the two percentages and choose the report with the greatest combined evidence for rain.
strings.math.audit.prompt: This chapter's Rice ledger opened at {opening}, received {inflow}, and paid out {outflow}. What is the closing balance?
strings.math.crisis.famine.prompt: Distribute {total} Rice among three districts in a ratio of {ratio0}:{ratio1}:{ratio2}.
strings.math.crisis.rebellion.prompt: Relief requires {percent}% of a {whole}-Treasury fund. How much Treasury is assigned to relief?
strings.math.crisis.flood.prompt: A flooded rectangle is {length} by {width} sections. At {materialsPerSquare} Materials per square section, how many Materials reinforce it?
strings.math.crisis.plague.prompt: Clinics and isolation houses need {percent}% of the {whole}-Treasury relief budget. How much Treasury goes to the clinics?
strings.math.crisis.raid.prompt: A depot is {length} sections long and {width} sections wide. One Material builds one section of palisade. How many Materials enclose the depot?
strings.math.battle.provision.prompt: One whole Rice ration supports up to {troopsPerRice} soldiers for one battle round. Rations cannot be shared between formations. Divide each formation’s soldiers by {troopsPerRice} and round UP to a whole ration; keep exact whole-number results unchanged. Add those rations, then multiply by {rounds} rounds. How much Rice is required?
strings.math.battle.warchest.prompt: The war chest holds {opening} Treasury. You selected {itemCount} equipment points at {itemCost} each. How much remains?
strings.hint.ratio.total_parts: Add the ratio parts to find how many equal shares the total contains.
strings.hint.ratio.find_one_part: Divide the total by the number of ratio parts, then multiply that share for each group.
strings.hint.percent.as_fraction: Write the percent as that many parts out of 100.
strings.hint.percent.multiply_then_divide: Multiply the whole by the percent, then divide by 100.
strings.hint.area.length_width: Find the rectangular area by multiplying length by width.
strings.hint.unit_rate.divide_coverage: After finding the area, divide by the number one bundle covers.
strings.hint.unit_rate.multiply: Multiply the number of units by the amount needed for each unit.
strings.hint.allocation.check_total: Add your allocations. They must equal the full amount available.
strings.hint.supply.per_formation: Add the issued Rice amounts in the schedule. Do not recalculate them from troop counts.
strings.hint.supply.round_each_formation: Round each formation separately; do not round only the combined army.
strings.hint.supply.multiply_periods: After finding the one-period need, multiply by the number of periods.
strings.hint.perimeter.all_sides: A perimeter includes both lengths and both widths.
strings.hint.perimeter.double_sum: Add length and width, then double that sum.
strings.hint.table.remove_unaffordable: First remove every plan that exceeds the available budget.
strings.hint.unit_rate.compare: Compare gain/cost exactly: for a/b and c/d, compare a × d with c × b. No decimal rounding is needed.
strings.hint.rate.distance_over_rate: Time equals distance divided by distance traveled each day.
strings.hint.elapsed.check_units: The distance units cancel, leaving days.
strings.hint.budget.find_lots: Divide the budget by the cost of one complete lot.
strings.hint.unit_rate.multiply_lots: Multiply the number of complete lots by the amount in each lot.
strings.hint.percent.find_first: Calculate the named percentage of the full amount first.
strings.hint.remainder.subtract: Subtract the first allocation or purchase from the total.
strings.hint.table.multiply_percent_pairs: For each report, multiply reliability by predicted rain.
strings.hint.table.compare_products: The greatest product represents the strongest combined evidence in this model.
strings.hint.ledger.add_inflow: Add the inflow to the opening balance.
strings.hint.ledger.subtract_outflow: Subtract the outflow from the amount available.
strings.hint.budget.total_cost: Multiply the number of equipment points by the cost of each point.

strings.ending.good.title: The Realm Pacified
strings.ending.good.opening: Victory was not won by numbers alone, but by making those numbers serve a coherent realm. Stores endured, commitments held, and the army reached the field able to act.
strings.ending.normal.title: A Narrow Ascendancy
strings.ending.normal.opening: The crisis has passed, but its cost is written in empty stores, strained promises, or formations that returned diminished. Authority survives, though peace remains unfinished.
strings.ending.bad.title: The Realm Divides Again
strings.ending.bad.opening: The campaign ends without the strength needed to impose a durable settlement. Shortage, disorder, broken commitments, or defeat leaves the realm open to another struggle.
strings.epilogue.crises_mastered: When disruption came, the administration met it with stores, labor, and figures already prepared.
strings.epilogue.crises_unanswered: Unanswered crises left damaged roads and unsettled districts behind the army's advance.
strings.epilogue.granaries_full: The granaries remained deep enough to support both the march and the households that supplied it.
strings.epilogue.granaries_empty: The army's road west was traced through granaries left nearly bare.
strings.epilogue.fair_register: A corrected register made revenue more dependable without demanding a harsher rate from every household.
strings.epilogue.hard_taxation: High levies filled the war chest, but their memory remained in the districts after the banners passed.
strings.epilogue.coalition_resolute: The Eastern houses reached Mino with their promises strengthened by repeated proof.
strings.epilogue.coalition_fractured: The coalition marched under one name, but not with one confidence.
strings.epilogue.kobayakawa_east: At the moment of decision, the uncertain auxiliary entered on the Eastern side.
strings.epilogue.kobayakawa_inactive: One uncertain banner never entered the fighting, leaving both councils to reckon with its silence.
strings.epilogue.kobayakawa_west: The uncertain auxiliary entered against Ieyasu, turning earlier diplomatic neglect into battlefield danger.
strings.epilogue.road_restored: Repairs ordered long before the crisis carried food, messages, and formations when speed mattered most.
strings.epilogue.road_broken: A damaged route slowed every solution that depended upon it.
strings.epilogue.homeland_guarded: Edo remained guarded while the field army moved beyond it.
strings.epilogue.homeland_exposed: The home districts paid for an army committed far from their defenses.
strings.epilogue.army_supplied: Supply held through the decisive rounds, preserving tactics that hunger would have closed.
strings.epilogue.army_starved: Once the prepared Rice was gone, morale and movement failed together.
strings.epilogue.measured_command: The field was won without spending every formation beyond recovery.
strings.epilogue.costly_victory: Victory came, but the surviving formations made its price impossible to hide.
strings.ui.rotate_device: Turn the iPad to landscape to continue. Your campaign is safe.
strings.ending.defeat.title: The Field Is Lost
strings.ending.defeat.opening: Sekigahara ends with the Western banners still standing. Your home domain survives, and with it the means to fight another year, but the Eastern coalition must now bargain rather than command.
strings.ending.withdrawal.title: A Withdrawal to Fight Again
strings.ending.withdrawal.opening: You pulled the army back before it broke. No one will call Sekigahara a victory, but the formations that marched home can still defend the realm while both coalitions count their losses.
strings.ending.v03.convoy.intact: The first grain convoy arrived intact. Its reward gave the council more resources for the road ahead.
strings.ending.v03.convoy.damaged: The relief convoy arrived damaged, but its remaining grain sustained the realm.
strings.ending.v03.convoy.lost: The early convoy was lost. The council continued without the expected cargo.
strings.ending.v03.convoy.skipped: The council left the early escort to other hands and governed without its cargo reward.
strings.ending.v03.plan.standard: The army fought in a standard line, retaining its available defensive preparations.
strings.ending.v03.plan.flanking: The prepared road and access through Gifu brought your reserve onto the field.
strings.ending.v03.plan.engineer: Your engineering investment opened a new crossing that either army could use.
strings.ending.v03.plan.fire_discipline: Equipped gun crews used disciplined suppressing fire to restrict the enemy.
strings.ending.v03.plan.unused: Your selected tactical opportunity remained unused; the outcome came from the orders you actually gave.
strings.ending.v03.outcome.camp_held: The battle ended after two consecutive uncontested camp-hold checks.
strings.ending.v03.outcome.core_rout: The battle ended when a coalition could no longer keep its main formations fighting.
strings.ending.v03.outcome.accepted_score: You accepted the battle council’s assessment of control, broken formations and remaining strength.
strings.ending.v03.outcome.withdrawal: You ended the battle by ordering a withdrawal.
strings.ending.v03.outcome.legacy_result: This result preserves the battle already completed in the earlier campaign.
